sections.body: DEMAND is how much of something people want to buy at different prices. Usually, when the price goes up, people buy less.
SUPPLY is how much sellers want to sell at different prices. Usually, when the price goes up, sellers want to sell more.
The market price tends to settle where the amount people want to buy matches the amount offered: the EQUILIBRIUM.
If demand rises (a product goes viral) and supply stays the same, prices tend to rise. If supply rises (a huge harvest), prices tend to fall.
Real markets are messier: governments set rules and taxes, some sellers have lots of power, and people don't always act 'rationally'. Economists debate how much these matter.
Think of a product that suddenly became popular. What happened to its price and why?

quiz.q: A bad harvest cuts the coffee supply, but demand stays the same. What tends to happen to the price?
hints: Less is available, but the same number of people want it.
When something becomes scarcer, what happens to the price?
Concert tickets: few seats and many fans means higher prices. Apply the same logic.
quiz.explain: Less supply with the same demand usually pushes the price up.

options: The amount buyers want equals the amount sellers offer
Prices are as high as possible
hints: Think about buyers and sellers meeting.
If 100 people want lemonade at 1 coin and 100 cups are offered at 1 coin, the market 'clears'. What's that point called?
quiz.explain: Equilibrium is where the amount demanded equals the amount supplied.

quiz.q: A farmers' market has far too many tomatoes at the end of the day. Sellers will most likely…
hints: How do sellers attract more buyers?
Shops have sales on winter coats in spring when too many are left. Why?
quiz.explain: With too much supply, sellers usually cut prices to attract buyers.
